examples.text: On a passé deux heures à pinailler sur la rédaction de ce tract.
examples.translation: We hebben twee uur zitten kommaneuken bij het opstellen van dat pamflet.

glosses: S’attarder sur des détails sans intérêt, argumenter avec des précisions superflues, de façon mesquine.

examples.text: On ne va tout de même pas pinailler pour si peu !
Quand tu auras fini de pinailler, nous parlerons sérieusement.
Il pinaillait sans cesse, à propos de tout et de rien, sans jamais emporter le morceau.
Il n’était pas de ceux qui pinaillent, qui tergiversent, qui mégotent. Les petits-bras, les mesquins, les frileux.

glosses: To correct insignificant mistakes or find fault in unimportant details.

examples.text: Someone will invariably nitpick about any spelling error posted to the forums.

But Pirates! comes with all the usual Aardman strengths intact, particularly the sense that its characters and creators alike are too good-hearted and sweet to nitpick. The ambition is all in the craft rather than in the storytelling, but it’s hard to say no to the proficiency of that craft, or the mild good cheer behind it.

glosses: To pick nits (lice eggs) from someone’s hair.
To pick nits (lice eggs) from someone’s hair.\nI nitpicked his hair.
I nitpicked his hair.
Tedious details; minutiae.

examples.text: The Microsoft trial had been in danger of slipping out of the public eye. Its endless procession of less-than-riveting economics professors and forgetful executives, mixed with scads of legal and technical split hairs, just hasn't made for gripping headlines.

glosses: To consider or argue about fine details; to worry about minutiae.

examples.text: Let's get everything sorted into the right drawers and not split hairs about subdividing it further yet.

glosses: An argument or objection based on an ambiguity of wording or similar trivial circumstance; a minor complaint.

examples.text: He harped on his quibble about how the dark red paint should be described as carmine rather than burgundy.
Quibbles […]have no place in the search after truth.
Toward the end of “Galatea,” there are a few missteps: […] All in all, though, these are minor quibbles.

glosses: A pun.

examples.text: Is it a quibble, or play upon words?

glosses: To complain or argue in a trivial or petty manner.

examples.text: They are constantly quibbling over insignificant details.
“Oh, if you talk in that sense!” said Mr. Standish, with as much disgust at such non-legal quibbling as a man can well betray towards a valuable client.

Mr. Musk has shown a disdain toward Twitter’s previous corporate culture. He has quibbled with the number of bird references in the company’s internal team names and products.

glosses: To contest, especially some trivial issue in a petty manner.

examples.text: The customer quibbled the bill.

glosses: To criticise for petty or frivolous reasons.

examples.text: 'Tis love you cavil at: I am not Love.

glosses: A petty or trivial objection or criticism.

examples.text: It is not worth while to spend your time in arguing against a cavil, but make him feel he is committing a sin to plead it, and thus enlist his conscience on your side.

glosses: Any of various freshwater fish of the family Cyprinidae; specifically the common carp, Cyprinus carpio.

examples.text: The Carp is a ſtately, a good, and a ſubtle fiſh, a fiſh that hath not (as it is ſaid) been long in England, but ſaid to be by one Mr. Maſcall (a Gentleman then living at Plumſted in Suſſex) brought into this Nation: […] Carps and Loches are obſerved to breed ſeveral months in one year, vvhich moſt other fiſh do not, and it is the rather believed, becauſe you ſhall ſcarce or never take a Male Carp vvithout a Melt, or a Female vvithout a Roe or Spavvn; […]

glosses: To criticize or complain about a fault, especially for frivolous or petty reasons; to cavil.

examples.text: Here agayne Seruetto carpeth, yͭ God did beare the perſon of an Angel. As thoughe the Prophete did not confirme that whiche Moſes had ſaied: why doeſt thou aſke me of my name?
Enuie vvhy carpeſt thou my time is ſpent ſo ill, / And termſt my vvorkes fruites of an idle quill.
[W]ith your good countenance protect against the malice of euill mouthes, vvhich are alvvaies vvide open to carpe at and miſconstrue my ſimple meaning.

[I]f vve ſhould never cenſure vvithout great Reaſon or neceſſity, hovv ſeldom ſhould vve do it? […] [D]o vve not eagerly ſearch after, and greedily embrace all occaſions to do it? Is it not a pleaſant entertainment to us, to be carping and cavelling at any Body vve meet, at any thing vve ſee done?
My vvorthy friend, ne'er grudge an' carp, / Tho' Fortune uſe you hard an' ſharp; / Come, kittle up your moorland harp / VVi' gleeſome touch!

glosses: To speak, to talk; also, to talk about a subject in speech or writing.
To talk much but to little purpose; to chatter, to prattle.

examples.text: And some of them barke, / Clatter and carpe / Of that heresy arte / Called Wicleuista, / The deuelysshe dogmatista; […]

glosses: Of a bird: to sing; of a person (such as a minstrel): to sing or recite.

examples.text: Hys hart is to hy to haue any hap; / But for in his gamut carp that he can, / Lo, Jak wold be a jentylman!

glosses: To say or tell (something).
To find fault with (someone or something); to censure, to criticize.
